summary.text: Ami Bera is a Democratic physician who has represented the Sacramento area in the U.S. House since 2013 and is the party's nominee for re-election in California's 3rd Congressional District. Before Congress he was Sacramento County's Chief Medical Officer and a UC Davis School of Medicine administrator. He sits on the House Foreign Affairs and Intelligence committees, and his campaign materials emphasize health care, housing, jobs, Social Security and Medicare, and public safety.

paragraphs.text: Bera was born in Los Angeles on March 2, 1965, and raised in La Palma in Orange County, the son of Indian immigrants.
He attended California public schools through medical school, earning both a B.S. and an M.D. from UC Irvine; his official biography says he graduated from medical school in 1991.

He completed an internal medicine residency at California Pacific Medical Center, becoming chief resident, and then practiced in the Sacramento area, holding leadership roles with MedClinic Medical Group and serving as medical director of care management for Mercy Healthcare.

Bera later served as Sacramento County's Chief Medical Officer and then worked as clinical professor of medicine and associate dean for admissions and outreach at UC Davis; Wikipedia lists his clinical professorship as running from 2005 to 2012.
Bera challenged Republican Rep. Dan Lungren in 2010 and again in 2012, and in 2012 he defeated Lungren in the newly redrawn 7th District by 3.4 points to win his first term.
He won re-election in 2014 by 0.8 points over Republican Doug Ose in a race Ballotpedia rated a battleground, and again in 2016 over Republican Scott Jones and in 2018 over Republican Andrew Grant.
Bera has represented Sacramento County in the House since January 2013, and Ballotpedia lists him as running for re-election in 2026 in the 3rd District.

His official biography lists him as Ranking Member of the Foreign Affairs Subcommittee on East Asia and the Pacific, a member of the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, and a member of the New Democrat Coalition, and it describes him as the longest-serving Indian American in Congress.

The biography also says his office has helped return more than $23 million to local taxpayers and assisted more than 36,000 Sacramento County residents since 2013, and that he has lived in Sacramento County for over 30 years with his wife, Janine, a physician; they have a daughter, Sydra.
